questions.q: According to the summary, what is the biggest obstacle to getting promoted?
a: Bad communication skills
A lack of technical expertise
Not enough ambition
Too few industry contacts
questions.why: Lesson 1 cites research finding that poor communication is the largest barrier to advancement at work.

questions.q: What happens when nervous speakers rush their words?
a: They sound uncertain and may say something regrettable
They come across as energetic and convincing
They hold attention better than slower speakers
They finish before the audience loses interest
questions.why: Lesson 2 says fast speech under stress sounds more neurotic than confident and can harm your reputation.

questions.q: What did Tony Hayward's remark about wanting his life back cost him?
a: His job
A regulatory fine
The company's share price
A public apology tour
questions.why: Lesson 2 says his careless comment during the Gulf oil spill ended up costing him his position.

questions.q: How does the author suggest preparing for casual conversations?
a: Keep a list of common questions you can ask
Memorize a script for every likely topic
Avoid discussing work or family entirely
Always let the other person speak first
questions.why: Lesson 3 describes preparing a list of commonly asked questions about family, background or work.

questions.q: Which practice does the author recommend even though it feels awkward?
a: Role-playing conversations with friends and family
Recording yourself and watching it back
Reading your presentation aloud many times
Joining a public speaking club
questions.why: Lesson 3 says role-playing is awkward but works well for preparing talks and conversations.
